etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English mynisterie, borrowed from Old French menistere, in turn borrowed itself from Latin ministerium; equivalent to minister +‎ -y.

definitions.definition: Government department, at the administrative level normally headed by a minister (or equivalent rank, e.g. secretary of state), who holds it as portfolio, especially in a constitutional monarchy, but also as a polity
The complete body of government ministers (whether or not they are in cabinet) under the leadership of a head of government (such as a prime minister)
The active practice and education of the minister of a particular religion or faith.
(Christianity) The clergy of nonapostolic Protestant churches.
(Christianity) Work of a spiritual or charitable nature.
